    Summary and Schedule

    Intro to Programming, Part 2: Data and Security with Python is the second of two six-week, beginner Python micro-credentials from the Australian Data and Cyber Institute (ADCI). It is for people who have finished Part 1. You learn the Python skills used in both data science and cyber security: working with text, reading files and logs, checking data and files, and using NumPy, Pandas and Matplotlib to analyse data and report what you find. Each week takes 6 hours or less, so it fits around a full-time job.

    You learn from short videos, these lesson notes, and a practice task each week. You write and run all the code in PyCharm. Every dataset is synthetic: it was made for this course, and no real logs or personal information are used. The security content is defensive and analytical only: checking, detecting, hashing and reporting.

    Learning outcomes

    Part 2 meets the same four outcomes as Part 1, applied to data and security problems:

    • LO 1 Analyse and solve a problem, and implement the solution in a programming language. This is practised in every week’s build.
    • LO 2 Apply programming techniques: imperative and object-oriented work in Weeks 1 to 3, and vectorised and grouped operations in Weeks 4 and 5.
    • LO 3 Design and build a program to a specification. Each week’s practice task has a written checklist.
    • LO 4 Evaluate which tool or method suits a problem: a loop or an array in Week 4, and which chart to draw in Week 6.

    How each week works

    Each week is one episode in the menu. Open a week to see its parts: the week overview, the sections (such as 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3), the Concepts Bridge and the practice task. Every week follows the same blocks:

    Block Time What you do
    Watch 20 to 40 min Short videos listed on the week overview
    Read & practise 1.5 to 2 h The week’s sections: read, run every example, do the exercises
    Concepts Bridge 30 min One general idea that the Python lessons do not cover
    Build 2 h (3 h in Week 6) Your portfolio item: a practice task with starter code, a model solution and tests
    Quiz 15 min A short quiz, marked automatically

    Your portfolio for each week is submitted at the end of the week and marked by your tutor.

    • A computer (Windows, Mac or Linux) with Python 3.12 or newer and PyCharm, as in Part 1.

    You need the same two free programs as in Part 1: Python 3.12 or newer and PyCharm. This page is a short checklist. It also shows how to get the course files and which packages to install, and when.

    Software Setup

    Discussion

    What you need

    • Python 3.12 or newer from python.org. Check with python --version (Windows) or python3 --version (Mac and Linux).
    • PyCharm from jetbrains.com/pycharm. The core features are free, and everything in this course works in them.
    • Your own library.py and main.py from Part 1 Week 6. You add to them in Week 2.

    If you finished Part 1, you already have all of this.

    Get the course files

    Download the course zip file and unzip it into your Documents folder. It gives you an IntroToProgrammingPart2 folder with:

    • an assets folder with the synthetic data files the lessons use (files and data);
    • a weeks folder with the lesson code for each section, and each week’s practice task (starter file, model solution and tests).

    Open the IntroToProgrammingPart2 folder in PyCharm (File > Open). Keep the folder layout. The programs find their data files by their place in this folder, so they will not find them if you move them.

    Create a virtual environment

    A virtual environment is a private set of packages for one project. Week 4 explains what it is and why you want one. You can create it now, or when you reach Week 4:

    1. In PyCharm, open Settings > Project > Python Interpreter.
    2. Add a new interpreter and choose Virtualenv (a new environment in the project folder).
    3. Open the Terminal tab at the bottom of PyCharm. You should see (.venv) at the start of the line.

    Install packages when you need them

    Install each package with python -m pip install, in the PyCharm Terminal, with the virtual environment active.

    When Command What it is for
    Week 1 python -m pip install pytest Running the practice tests
    Week 4 python -m pip install numpy Arrays and statistics
    Week 5 python -m pip install pandas Tables of data
    Week 6 python -m pip install matplotlib Charts

    Installing only what you need keeps your project small. Check that the name is spelled exactly as shown before you press Enter.

    Data Sets

    Every data file in this course is synthetic. It was made for the course, and it contains no real logs and no personal information. The internet addresses in the logs come from ranges reserved for examples, so they belong to nobody.

    File Used in What it holds
    sample_text.txt Week 1 A short passage, “The Quiet Server Room”
    web_log.txt Week 2 200 web-server log lines over two days
    common_passwords.txt Week 3 50 common passwords, one on each line
    login_counts.csv Week 4 Daily login counts for six users over 28 days
    web_log.csv Week 5 The same 200 log records as a CSV file
    login_attempts.csv Week 6 Capstone option A: login attempts over two weeks
    sales.csv Week 6 Capstone option B: three months of sales for an invented shop
